title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week, funding continues to flow into the space sector, with notable investments from Chinese and American firms. Meanwhile, the U.S. military's focus on space resilience appears to be gaining traction, even as hypersonic testing remains stuck in a holding pattern.

themes.title: Funding Frenzy in Space
themes.body: Chinese satellite manufacturer Hongqing's $191 million raise highlights the ongoing investment interest in space technology. Meanwhile, True Anomaly's $190 million Series C round underscores a similar trend in the U.S. market.

themes.title: Military Space Resilience Gains
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup's additional $1.4 billion for space resilience indicates a growing recognition of the need for robust satellite communications. This comes alongside Anduril and L3Harris's tactical SDA constellation bid, suggesting a strategic pivot in defense priorities.

themes.title: Launch Contracts and Innovations
themes.body: Isar Aerospace's recent contract to launch a German-built Planet imaging satellite marks a significant step for European space capabilities. Additionally, Sierra Space's Dream Chaser DoD variant passing its critical design review signals progress in reusable space vehicles.

themes.title: The AI Defense Trend
themes.body: The surge of 'AI for Defense' startups, particularly among Y Combinator companies, reflects a broader trend of integrating advanced technologies into military applications. This could reshape the defense landscape, but the practical implications remain to be seen.
